subject: Performance SLO & Context Window follow-up - FinCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jack Turner <jack.turner@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & Context Window follow-up - FinCo

Hi Jack — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap + proposed next steps so we can move toward a short perf qualification: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for interactive assistant flows (single-turn generation).
- Throughput: baseline target 400 requests/minute with burst to 1,200 reqs/min.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~40, peak concurrency up to ~150.
- Streaming: required for multi-turn chat; we need server-side partial token streaming to the client (chunked responses).
- Context window: input up to 120k input tokens across recent convo + metadata; expected response up to 2k tokens in some cases.

Key performance considerations we discussed:
- Larger context windows (100k+ tokens) increase KV cache pressure and memory footprint; generation latency is dominated by attention/kv lookup for long prefixes.
- Output max_tokens (~2k) combined with streaming reduces tail latency for the first bytes but still requires compute proportional to output length for full response.
- Concurrency + long contexts will push us toward larger replicas or sharded KV serving; we should validate with your real payloads.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a representative sample of requests (we suggested a small .jsonl with 50-100 representative sessions) — we can use that to run a perf job.
2) Redwood runs a 2-hour perf profile against a Dedicated-like configuration and sends a latency/throughput report and recommended config (batch sizes, quantization profile, routing policy).
3) Align on SLA language and any required fallback policies (model variant or region).

I've attached a stub for the workload sample (finco_workload_sample.jsonl) and a draft SLA for your review (SLA-draft-FinCo-v1.docx).

Ask: can you confirm whether the 120k context window estimate is peak or typical? Also confirm if streaming to clients needs strict byte-level chunks (<200ms per chunk) or just token-level streaming is fine.

Thanks — will coordinate perf window after we get the sample.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: finco_workload_sample.jsonl (10KB stub)
Attachment: SLA-draft-FinCo-v1.docx (SLA draft, redlines welcome)

From: Jack Turner <jack.turner@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinCo Platform <platform@finco.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Context Window follow-up - FinCo

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 120k context window is a worst-case aggregate; typical sessions average ~35-45k tokens, but we have a small percentage (<5%) of sessions where we retain a long history and embeddings/meta causing ~100-120k. We want the system to handle the tail gracefully rather than fail.
- Streaming: we need token-level streaming where the client renders tokens as they arrive. We prefer chunk latency <200ms for the first chunk on cold requests; subsequent chunks can be relaxed slightly.
- Concurrency: 150 peak is for peak batch windows (end of day analytics + interactive spike). We can gate heavy history sessions with an internal policy, but we'd prefer Redwood to recommend an architectural stance (fallback smaller context or truncated context with salient extraction).

Attached a small sample set (we'll export a sanitized subset). For the perf run, can you also include a run that simulates: (A) 40 concurrent users with typical 40k context, (B) 40 concurrent users with 100k context to see delta, and (C) 150 concurrent users with mixed contexts? That will help us decide on reserved capacity sizing.

I'll aim to get the sanitized export by EOD tomorrow.

- Jack
Head of Platform
FinCo

--
Attachment: (Jack will provide sanitized sample by EOD tomorrow)

FYI forwarding Jack's response and next actions. Action items for infra/solutions: 

- Rishi: please schedule a perf qualification window for next week (2-hour slot) and prepare two configurations: 
  * Config A: Dedicated-like baseline (4x A100-equivalent) with quantization profile conservative (fp16/8-bit)
  * Config B: High-memory sharded serving for long-context (100k) - prioritize KV memory over batch size.
- Vivek: can you validate that our streaming path can provide first-byte <200ms on cold starts for median request with 40k context? If not, let's document expected warmup behavior and suggested mitigations (prefix caching, first-token warm cache).
- Rishi: request that Jack uploads sanitized finco_workload_sample.jsonl to the shared doc link; I've added our perf plan doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FinCoPerfPlan

I'll reply to Jack to confirm the perf matrix (A/B/C) and propose Wed/Thu next week windows.

Marissa

Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 18:45:00 -07:00

Thanks Marissa — I'll slot perf runs for Wed 03/31 and Thu 04/01 morning PT. Planning to run the three matrices Jack requested (A/B/C). Two quick questions: 

1) For the 100k context runs, do we simulate full document-history in the input or synthesize by duplicating context until we reach token target? Jack said sanitized export coming; if that's delayed, we'll use synthesized long-context test vectors but need note in report.
2) What max_output_tokens should we use for parity with FinCo? Jack mentioned ~2k; should we run both 512 and 2k to observe p95 behavior across short and long outputs?

I'll prepare run scripts and share raw CSV latency/throughput logs and a short slide deck with recommendations.

Rishi
